first_impression.reaction: Good. It answers my Google question in the first sentence and names two government sources. No 'dream wedding' fluff before the answer. I jumped straight to the FAQ like I always do, it held up, so I went back and read most of it properly.

journey.quote: In most cases, yes: an overseas marriage is generally recognised here if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law, according to both Smartraveller and the Attorney-General's Department.
journey.reaction: Straight answer, sourced, with the caveat built in. That's how I'd want a planner to talk to me.

journey.quote: This guide covers recognition, proof, surnames and later celebrations, as at October 2026.
journey.reaction: A date on legal info. Means I can tell if it's stale. Most wedding sites never bother.

journey.section: The legal test: what the Marriage Act says
journey.quote: The current text of [Part VA of the Marriage Act 1961](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C1961A00012/latest/text) is compilation No. 34, 28 March 2026.
journey.reaction: Section numbers and a compilation number I can check myself. I did click through mentally to legislation.gov.au. This is the kind of thing I'd verify, and they've made it easy.

journey.section: When an Italian marriage would not be recognised
journey.quote: For most couples none of this applies. The one to check is an earlier divorce, which must be final before the Italian ceremony.
journey.reaction: Useful. Tells me which of the four exceptions actually matters in real life instead of leaving me to work it out.

journey.section: Marriage certificate, atto or multilingual extract
journey.quote: Not published: whether any Australian agency accepts an Italian multilingual extract on its own.
journey.reaction: Admitting what they don't know instead of bluffing. That's the single biggest trust builder on the page for me.

journey.quote: Not published: Prefettura processing times. Ask your Wedded Advisor to build the appointment into your plan.
journey.reaction: First half is honest. Second half is a sales nudge dropped into a legal explainer. Minor, but I noticed it. What does the Advisor actually do here, book it, or just remind me?

journey.quote: Its name-change page lists an Australian marriage certificate, or original Home Affairs evidence if you changed your name overseas; whether it accepts an apostilled Italian certificate is not published
journey.reaction: Fine, but it leaves me with homework. Still, better than someone telling me it'll be fine.

journey.quote: You may not be able to take your partner's name automatically; some organisations need an official change of name
journey.reaction: I'm in Brisbane, so this is the row I care about, and it's the vaguest. 'May not' and 'some organisations'. Which ones? What does a Queensland change of name cost and how long does it take? NSW and Victoria got their own subsection, Queensland got one hedge.

journey.section: The trade-offs if Italy should be 'the' wedding
journey.quote: The cost is emotional. Your legal anniversary becomes a short ceremony at home, and some couples feel the Italian vows repeat something already done.
journey.reaction: Points for naming the downside of the option that's easier for a planner to sell. Though 'the cost' made me expect an actual cost. The admin-saving side has real dollar and time savings they don't quantify either way.

journey.section: Same-sex couples: Italian civil unions and Australian law
journey.quote: A civil union is a different thing, and no Australian government page we found says how an Italian one is treated here.
journey.reaction: Honest about a gap rather than glossing it. Not my situation, but it tells me how they'd handle a question they can't answer.

journey.section: Get the legal side settled before you book
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person from first idea to the last dance, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, and confirms in writing what is included before you commit.
journey.reaction: 'Confirms in writing what is included' is the right instinct. 'First idea to the last dance' is brochure talk. And nothing on how the Advisor is paid. Fee? Percentage? Commission from the comune's venues? That's my actual question and it's not here.

journey.section: Get the legal side settled before you book
journey.quote: Requirements change, so your Wedded Advisor confirms the current requirements for your dates before you book. It is not legal advice; for your own circumstances, speak with a family lawyer.
journey.reaction: Slightly mixed message. The Advisor 'confirms the current requirements' but it's 'not legal advice'. So who's on the hook if the Advisor confirms something wrong? I'd ask that on a call.

unanswered_questions: What does the paperwork actually cost: apostille, NAATI translation, a Queensland change of name? Even rough official fees would help me budget.
What exactly does Queensland require for a surname change after an overseas marriage, and how long does it take?
How is a Wedded Advisor paid: flat fee, percentage, or commissions from venues and suppliers?
Does the Advisor physically book the Prefettura appointment and arrange the translation, or just tell us to do it? Is that included or extra?
If the Advisor 'confirms the current requirements' and gets it wrong, who carries that risk?
Roughly how much admin time and cost does marrying in Australia first save versus a legal Italian wedding?

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person from first idea to the last dance
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional brochure phrasing at the exact point I want facts about what the service costs and covers.

turn_offs_found.quote: Ask your Wedded Advisor to build the appointment into your plan.
turn_offs_found.why: Sales mention inside an otherwise neutral legal section, and it doesn't say what the Advisor actually does or whether it costs extra.

would_share_with: My fiancee, as the reference for the paperwork side
Possibly a Reddit thread if someone asks the same question, because it cites the Act and government pages

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [speak with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge) about which route suits you.
cta_reaction.why: The article earned some credibility, and the CTA sits after the evidence, not before it, which I respect. But clicking means a sales conversation, and I still don't know the fee model. I'd look for a pricing or 'how we're paid' page first. If that exists and is clear, I'd book a call.

top_3_changes: Give Queensland (and the other non-NSW/VIC states) something concrete: what form, roughly what fee, roughly how long, with the registry link. 'May not' and 'some organisations' isn't enough.
Where the Advisor is mentioned, say plainly what they do (book the Prefettura slot? arrange translation?) and link to how the fee works. Swap 'first idea to the last dance' for that.
Add rough official costs for the apostille, NAATI translation and a change of name, dated and sourced, so I can compare the two routes in dollars, not just feelings.
